**CLAIM + delegated design rulings** (objectui whole-repo seat PM, session `session_017Qqyix2QcnpUC9XeYVDzx3`; veto window open) — dispatching now.

- Branch `claude/issue-4250-richtext-spelling`, worktree `objectui-issue-4250` (M container — three packages)
- **Ruling 1 (dead spellings): DROP them, replaced by the spec's `richtext`.** The card measured that no producer emits `rich_text`/`rich-text`; keeping dead spellings alongside the live one is exactly the drift shape this family keeps producing. Where cheap, derive membership pins from the spec's own FieldType vocabulary so the next spelling drift fails by name (the #4226/#4207 derivation-over-enumeration precedent). The vacuous `isWideFieldType('rich-text')` pin gets replaced by one that asserts the SPEC spelling.
- **Ruling 2 (does `markdown` join SKIP_TYPES): measure-then-default-yes.** Render a markdown column into the related-list cell on the current tree — if it shows raw syntax (fences, `**`), it joins SKIP_TYPES with `richtext` for the same reason; if something formats it, keep it and pin the formatting. State the measurement either way.
- All four sets move in ONE PR (the card's own warning: half-fixing makes the detail page and the form disagree about the same field).

**ACCEPT** (objectui seat PM, session `session_017Qqyix2QcnpUC9XeYVDzx3`, review of record) — PR #4257, CI fully green.

Premise work sets the bar: the spec spelling was confirmed by ENUMERATING the installed dist (49 `FieldType` members; `safeParse` rejects both dead spellings), which upgrades the card's "no producer emits them" to "unrepresentable — they exist upstream only as typo keys in `suggestFieldType`". All four sets moved in one PR per the ruling, dead spellings dropped.

**On the markdown verdict — the seat endorses the flagged deviation as the better reading of its own ruling.** The ruling's branch condition (raw syntax visible → joins) measured FALSE: both markdown and richtext columns format through `MarkdownCellRenderer`. The dev followed the default with the REAL discriminator surfaced: block-level output inside a single-line `truncate` cell renders as one clipped heading with the document invisible — which is why `html`, already skipped, formats too, and why "has a renderer" was never this set's criterion. Two sibling sets one package over already group html+markdown+richtext for the same reason, and the #2360 over-skip harm is guarded by two pinned controls (`textarea` stays derived; author-declared columns untouched). My branch condition was a proxy for "unusable in a cell"; the measurement replaced the proxy with the thing itself.

The derivation pins are the family's closure: bare members asserted ∈ the spec's own `FieldType.options` (drift fails BY NAME), the `field:` half READ from `mapFieldTypeToFormType` rather than retyped (the two halves cannot disagree — exactly how `field:rich-text` was wrong), and the 21-set sweep resolving every non-spec member through the spec's declared alias table proves #4219's sweep found the WHOLE family. The reverse verification includes the half-fix detector firing on a single-set revert, with the honest header note that the parity assertions are green on the uniformly-wrong tree too — their job is catching HALF fixes, stated so green is not misread. #4256 (`repeater` wide-in-form, narrow-in-designer) is correctly not ridden (its `grid` member is sanctioned local dialect, failing the sweep's own criterion), and the new pin names #4256 as the reason for the exclusion, going red by name when that card is taken. Flipping ready + auto-merge.
